task: T2: give the harness two SEARCH PATHS so a repo that is not this one needs to vendor nothing, in scripts/run-loop.sh and in the per-task gates. First, strategies: resolve <name>.conf from $HARNESS_REPO_ROOT/.harness/loops/ before $SCRIPT_DIR/loops/, first match wins, so a consumer repo can both add strategies and shadow a built-in one. Export HARNESS_REPO_ROOT — the git toplevel of the repo being worked on — BEFORE the line that sources the conf: a conf cannot use $ROOT because ralph-build.sh is what exports ROOT and it has not run yet at that point, which is precisely the bug a consumer conf would hit first and the reason this ordering is an acceptance criterion rather than an implementation detail. Extend --list to show strategies from both locations with which is which, and to NOT list a built-in that a consumer conf shadows, since showing both names would tell a reader the opposite of what will run; when a strategy is found in neither, exit non-zero naming BOTH searched paths rather than the old single-path message. Second, the assertion vocabulary: every per-task gate opens with `. "$ROOT/specs/lib/assert.sh"` where ROOT is the WORKED repo, so a repo that follows the convention — specs and gates, no harness — must still carry a copy of assert.sh that then drifts from the harness's. Resolve $HARNESS_HOME/specs/lib/assert.sh first with the $ROOT path as fallback, and update the existing gates' source line to the resolved form; in this repo both paths point at the same file, so every existing gate must still pass unchanged, and that is the check that this did not quietly break the harness's own tests. Fallback-first throughout, in the shape ralph-build.sh's per-task gate resolver already established: a repo with no .harness/ directory and no HARNESS_HOME set is not misconfigured, it is every repo that exists today. Do not add STRATEGY_TOOLS here — T3 owns it — and do not touch any exec-*.sh binding.
